text:
Montreal led 3-2 after one period and 3-3 after the first half of the second, and nothing about the way Carolina played changed in between. The Hurricanes outshot the Canadiens 33-20, attempted 68 shots to 38, and generated 4.92 expected goals to Montreal's 2.41. Replay every shot a thousand times and Carolina wins about 73 percent of them. The early deficit was mostly a product of Montreal's finishing: Nick Suzuki's snap shot at 4:27 of the first carried a 6 percent chance of going in, and Zachary Bolduc's backhand a minute earlier was 34 percent.

Carolina's edge widened from there. The Hurricanes outchanced Montreal 1.63 to 0.35 in the second, where Sebastian Aho tied it on the power play at 3:56 and Mark Jankowski put Carolina ahead at 13:24 on a backhand off a feed from Eric Robinson. Taylor Hall finished with two goals and four shots, and his second, at 12:21 of the third, made it 5-3. Aho added two assists and led all skaters at 2.52 expected goals for while on the ice, and Jaccob Slavin, who logged 21:19, picked up two helpers.

Montreal did not go quietly. Juraj Slafkovský cut it to 5-4 at 16:57, and the Canadiens pushed to 1.22 expected goals in the third, their best period. But Andrei Svechnikov's snap shot at 18:45 carried an 87 percent chance of scoring, a plain tap-in that ended it. Neither goalie had a good night against the shot quality they faced: Jakub Dobes allowed 1.19 more goals than expected, and Brandon Bussi 1.59 more. Carolina simply made the better case, shot after shot.
